turns.utterance: Starting spindle diagnostic procedure.

ground_truth.node_text: Start

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Begin with a warm-up run. Bring the spindle up to 50% speed and let it run for 10 minutes.

ground_truth.node_text: Warm up run, spindle at 50% speed for 10 minutes

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Warm-up complete. Spindle has been running at 50% speed for the full 10 minutes.

ground_truth.node_text: Warm up run, spindle at 50% speed for 10 minutes

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Mount a calibrated accelerometer on the front bearing housing using a flat washer stud or magnetic base. Run the spindle at 3000 RPM with no toolholder fitted and record the RMS vibration velocity in millimeters per second. Then repeat at maximum rated speed and compare both readings against the ISO 10816 zone limits for this machine class.

ground_truth.node_text: Mount a calibrated accelerometer on the front bearing housing with a flat washer stud or magnetic base. Run the spindle at 3000 revolutions per minute with no toolholder fitted and record the root mean square vibration velocity in millimetres per second. Repeat at the maximum rated speed and compare both readings against the ISO 10816 zone limits for this machine class.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Accelerometer mounted and readings taken. At 3000 RPM I'm getting 1.8 millimeters per second, and at max speed it's 2.1 millimeters per second. Both are within the ISO zone limits.

ground_truth.node_text: Mount a calibrated accelerometer on the front bearing housing with a flat washer stud or magnetic base. Run the spindle at 3000 revolutions per minute with no toolholder fitted and record the root mean square vibration velocity in millimetres per second. Repeat at the maximum rated speed and compare both readings against the ISO 10816 zone limits for this machine class.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the vibration level below the alarm limit?

ground_truth.node_text: Vibration level below alarm limit?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, both readings are well below the alarm threshold. We're in the acceptable zone.

ground_truth.node_text: Vibration level below alarm limit?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the bearing temperature within the rated operating limit?

ground_truth.node_text: Bearing temperature within rated operating limit?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Temperature is good. Front bearing is at 18 degrees above ambient and rear is at 20 degrees, both well under the 25 degree rise limit.

ground_truth.node_text: Bearing temperature within rated operating limit?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the radial runout within 2 micrometer tolerance?

ground_truth.node_text: Radial runout within 2 µm tolerance?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, I'm reading 3.2 micrometers total indicator reading on the spindle nose. That's over the 2 micrometer spec.

ground_truth.node_text: Radial runout within 2 µm tolerance?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Adjust the bearing preload via the locknut in quarter-turn increments.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust bearing pre load via locknut, quarter turn increments

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Preload adjusted. I've tightened the locknut a quarter turn and checked the feel.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust bearing pre load via locknut, quarter turn increments

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Reverify the radial runout after the preload adjustment.

ground_truth.node_text: Reverify radial runout after pre load adjustment

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Still showing 2.9 micrometers. The adjustment helped a bit but we're still out of spec.

ground_truth.node_text: Reverify radial runout after pre load adjustment

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Perform supplementary bearing preload correction. Disassemble the spindle nose bearing housing, remove the preload spacer, and replace it with a spacer from the next shim increment in the bearing service kit. Reassemble to the specified torque and run the spindle at 1000 RPM for 10 minutes to allow the bearings to seat.

ground_truth.node_text: Supplementary bearing preload correction: disassemble the spindle nose bearing housing, remove the preload spacer, and replace it with a spacer from the next shim increment in the bearing service kit. Reassemble the housing to the specified torque and run the spindle at 1000 revolutions per minute for 10 minutes to allow bearings to seat before returning to the runout measurement step.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Housing disassembled, spacer replaced with the next increment, and reassembled to torque spec. I've run it at 1000 RPM for 10 minutes and the bearings have seated.

ground_truth.node_text: Supplementary bearing preload correction: disassemble the spindle nose bearing housing, remove the preload spacer, and replace it with a spacer from the next shim increment in the bearing service kit. Reassemble the housing to the specified torque and run the spindle at 1000 revolutions per minute for 10 minutes to allow bearings to seat before returning to the runout measurement step.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Reverify the radial runout after the preload adjustment.

ground_truth.node_text: Reverify radial runout after pre load adjustment

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Still reading 2.7 micrometers. After the second attempt with the shim replacement, we're still above tolerance.

ground_truth.node_text: Reverify radial runout after pre load adjustment

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Procedure complete. Escalate immediately: runout is unrecoverable and bearing replacement is required. Take the spindle offline and notify the maintenance team for bearing service.

ground_truth.node_text: End, Escalate: runout unrecoverable, bearing replacement required

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Understood. I'll tag the machine out and escalate to the bearing service team right away.

ground_truth.node_text: End, Escalate: runout unrecoverable, bearing replacement required
